issue.title: feat(experimental-react): ssr: false for queries only a browser can run
issue.body: ## Stack | PR | What | | --- | --- | | [#8031](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/8031) | Keep what changes while a request is in flight | | 👉 **this** | `ssr: false` for queries only a browser can run | ## Why - A query the server can't run (the browser's session, `localStorage` in its input) had no way to stay off the server. `.query()` in a server render started it anyway. ## What ```ts const post = trpc.post.byId.query({ id }, { ssr: false }); ``` - On a server store, without data, it starts nothing. Its promise rejects with an error whose `digest` is `BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING` (the one Next.js gives `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`), so `use()` renders the Suspense fallback and the browser renders the boundary. - It's the entry's own promise, so `useQuery` reads it; a later read without `ssr: false` starts the request. - On a browser store it changes nothing. New types: `ReadOptions`, `ReactQueryArgs`. ## Links - [`experimental-react.md` › Server rendering](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/feat/react-ssr-false/www/v12/docs/integrations/experimental-react.md): new paragraph and example. Preview URLs not generated here. ## Alternatives considered - A `skipToken`-style sentinel (TanStack): it disables the query everywhere, but the browser should still run it. ## Testing - `dom.test.tsx`: "ssr: false: the server renders the fallback and sends nothing…" fails without it (the server render requests the post). ## AI model Claude, via Claude Code. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_019Un67eXJphvS2ZoXwSMsBt)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? fix(experimental-react): keep what changes while a request is in flight
issue.body:
## Stack

| PR | What |
| --- | --- |
| 👉 **this** | Keep what changes while a request is in flight |
| [#8032](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/8032) | `ssr: false` for queries only a browser can run |

## Why

- A request's answer overwrote the entry when it landed. A `setData` (optimistic update) made during a background refetch flipped back to older data.
- An `invalidate()` during a request joined it, and its older answer cleared the invalidation. A mutation could resolve showing data read before it.

## What

- A `setData` or `hydrate` write made while a request runs keeps its data; the late answer is dropped. A first load in flight settles with the write.
- An invalidation made while a request runs leaves its answer stale. `invalidate()` waits for it, then refetches the entries on screen, and resolves after that.
- Fixes a flaky dom test that invalidated before React's mount effect ran (separate commit).

## Links

- [`experimental-react.md` › Cache methods](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/fix/react-keep-writes-during-requests/www/v12/docs/integrations/experimental-react.md): one paragraph. Preview URLs not generated here.

## Alternatives considered

- Abort the request in flight on `invalidate()`: it would also drop the request a loader shares.

## Testing

- `index.test.ts`: "a write made while a request is in flight keeps its data over the late answer" fails without the fix.
